models.name: ai_shop_carts
models.description:
Shopping Cart Entity - Implements the persistent cart requirement from the Cart and Order System document (Section 4, Functional Requirements #1, #3).

This model represents a logical shopping cart associated primarily with a customer or a guest session. Its business purpose is to enable the platform to store a user's intended purchases across sessions, devices, and authentication states. It ensures 3NF normalization by storing only the cart container and its metadata; specific cart item details are normalized into ai_shop_cart_items. For example, when a customer adds products to their shopping cart, this entity records the top-level cart record, trackable by customer_id or cart_session_id.

Key relationships: Links to ai_shop_cart_sessions (if unauthenticated), and to ai_shop_customers (for authenticated users; foreign key to be defined from Actors schema). Maintains audit fields and status for cart lifecycle (active, abandoned, converted, etc).
Special behaviors: Cart is unique to either a customer or a session, never both, supporting both registered and guest flows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each shopping cart.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_shop_customers.id}. Nullable for guest carts. This links a shopping cart directly to a registered customer account for persistent, cross-device cart experience.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_cart_session_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged cart session's {@link ai_shop_cart_sessions.id}. Used for unauthenticated/guest carts.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Cart status flag - Implements the requirement for lifecycle tracking (active, abandoned, converted). Business meaning: tracks the primary cart state for abandonment processing and analytic triggers. Normalized here as a single atomic value. E.g., 'active', 'abandoned'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Cart creation timestamp. Used for audit trails and tracking cart staleness/abandonment for compliance and customer service. 3NF-compliant atomic timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Cart last updated timestamp. Enables precise cart lifecycle management, normalization preserved.

plainFields.name: abandoned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the cart was considered abandoned. Implements compliance and business abandonment requirements. Nullable as only set when cart is abandoned.

models.name: ai_shop_cart_items
models.description:
Shopping Cart Item Entity - Implements the normalized itemization requirement from Cart and Order System document (Functional Requirements #1, #3, #4).

This entity stores each product/variant line in a shopping cart, supporting full 3NF normalization. Business purpose: allows for precise separation of cart container and contained product selections. For example, each entry represents a single SKU/variant the customer intends to buy, with quantity and option/variant references.

Key relationships: Belongs to ai_shop_carts, references ai_shop_products and ai_shop_product_variants (from Products schema) to ensure referential integrity for catalog links. Normalized: NO product names/prices stored here. Example usage: add-to-cart API inserts a record per selected product variant, quantity, and options. Special behaviors: Each cart can have many items, each item unique by product/variant constraints.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each cart item.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_cart_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged cart's {@link ai_shop_carts.id}. Links item to its parent cart for proper containment and lifecycle management.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product reference's {@link ai_shop_products.id}. Enforces product-level referential integrity. Normalized - only stores reference, not product data.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Product variant reference's {@link ai_shop_product_variants.id}. Ensures atomic relationship at SKU/variant granularity. No denormalized attribute data.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of the product variant requested. Implements the atomic, normalized representation of product choices. Always ≥ 1. E.g., user selects 2 of a certain size/color.

plainFields.name: added_at
plainFields.description: When the cart item was added. Business purpose: enables time-based cart, inventory, and promotional analytics. Maintains normalization as atomic value.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for cart item. Useful for tracking changes (e.g., quantity updates). Still atomic and normalized.

models.name: ai_shop_cart_sessions
models.description:
Cart Session Entity - Addresses the session-linked cart requirement from Cart and Order System (Functional Requirement #1 and architectural needs).

Business purpose: enables persistent cart storage for unauthenticated/guest users using a session-unique token. Maintains normalization by only recording the link to the guest session. When a user logs in, their session cart can be migrated to their account cart. For example, a new visitor adds items to a cart and is tracked via this record until authentication. Audit trail fields enable lifecycle and analytic monitoring.

Key relationships: Optionally linked to ai_shop_carts (1:1), not directly to products or customers. Used for session-based cart flows. Special behaviors: Carts can be migrated/merged between guest sessions and user accounts based on business rules.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this cart session.

plainFields.name: session_token
plainFields.description: Unique session token issued to guest/unregistered users to identify cart sessions. Implements guest cart persistence. Atomic value; not reused or denormalized.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation time for the cart session. Audit/compliance requirement.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update time for the session's activity/lifecycle. Enables analysis and cart synchronization.

models.name: ai_shop_orders
models.description: Order entity - This implements the primary order management requirement from the Cart and Order System requirements. Captures the full business-to-customer transaction lifecycle, including customer linkage, cart association, seller involvement, pricing, and order audit. 3NF compliance: Only atomic, normalized data (no pre-calculated totals). For example, when a customer checks out a cart, an ai_shop_orders record is created with all relevant FK links. Key relationships: Linked to ai_shop_customers, ai_shop_carts, ai_shop_sellers, and item, delivery, refund entities.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_shop_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller's {@link ai_shop_sellers.id} for single-seller orders, or main seller in multi-seller scenario

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_cart_id
foreignFields.description: Associated cart's {@link ai_shop_carts.id} for order provenance

plainFields.name: order_number
plainFields.description: Order human-readable identifier - Implements traceability for the business and customers. 3NF: not derived from other columns, strictly assigned at order creation. E.g. 'ORD20240722-0001'.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current order business status (e.g., pending, paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) - Implements state management. Not derived. Usage: for process control and audit.

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when order was placed - Implements audit/compliance requirements. Not derived data. Used to track order creation moment.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last updated timestamp - For auditing order state progression. Not derived; is updated by workflow actions.

plainFields.name: payment_method
plainFields.description: Selected payment method code (e.g., 'card', 'deposit', 'coupon'). Fulfills checkout and compliance requirement. Not derived from other entities.

plainFields.name: customer_memo
plainFields.description: Customer's memo for the order (e.g., delivery instructions) - Direct input, atomic, not derived.

plainFields.name: admin_note
plainFields.description: Internal admin memo about the order - 3NF: for audit/admin use only, not shown externally. Input only, not derived.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion flag: timestamp if deleted, null otherwise. For audit and compliance, enables logical deletes.

models.name: ai_shop_order_items
models.description: Order item detail - Implements the order line-items requirement from the Cart and Order System plan. Each row represents a distinct item within an order (SKU-level). Fully normalized (3NF): no derived subtotals or aggregates; each field corresponds directly to atomic input or reference. Used, for example, to list each purchased product with its variant, quantity, and price at purchase time. Key relationships: Foreign keys to ai_shop_orders and ai_shop_products/variants.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_id
foreignFields.description: Parent order's {@link ai_shop_orders.id} - Required for item linkage.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_product_id
foreignFields.description: Purchased product's {@link ai_shop_products.id} - 3NF; atomic reference for business reporting.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Variant of the product's {@link ai_shop_product_variants.id}. Enables SKU-level granularity and atomic normalization.

plainFields.name: product_name
plainFields.description: Snapshot of the product name at purchase. Implements audit/traceability. Not derived; direct input. Example: 'AI Smart Speaker v2'.

plainFields.name: variant_name
plainFields.description: Optional: Variant display name for audit. Not derived; direct.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of this product/variant purchased.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Unit price at time of purchase (after discounts, if any). Fulfills audit and compliance; no calculations, atomic only.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'KRW') at sale time. Required for international operations; not derived.

plainFields.name: seller_memo
plainFields.description: Memo field for seller-side item note. Not derived; audit use. Example: 'Special packing'.

models.name: ai_shop_order_status_histories
models.description: Order state change log - Implements the audit/compliance snapshot from requirements: logs every change in ai_shop_orders.status. Maintains full normalized snapshot history. For example, a new row is added whenever the order status transitions (e.g., from 'pending' to 'paid'). Key relationships: Foreign key to ai_shop_orders. Special behaviors: Immutable records, always append-only.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the affected {@link ai_shop_orders.id}. For access path and integrity.

foreignFields.name: changed_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Optional reference to admin who performed the update. For compliance and traceability ({@link ai_shop_admins.id}).

plainFields.name: from_status
plainFields.description: Previous status value - For audit trail, normalization 3NF: not derived.

plainFields.name: to_status
plainFields.description: New status value - For audit trail.

plainFields.name: changed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of change event. Not derived; audit evidence. Atomic property.

plainFields.name: change_reason
plainFields.description: Optional admin/editor reason for status change. Fulfills requirement for business auditing. Not derived.

models.name: ai_shop_order_refunds
models.description: Order refund request entity - Fulfills the requirement for explicit tracking of refund requests and processing from the requirements analysis. 3NF compliance: only atomic, factual attributes are stored for each refund. Used, for instance, when a buyer requests a refund for an order item. Key relationships: FK to ai_shop_orders.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_id
foreignFields.description: Refunded order's {@link ai_shop_orders.id}. For traceability and workflow enforcement.

foreignFields.name: requested_by_customer_id
foreignFields.description: FK to customer who requested refund ({@link ai_shop_customers.id}). Maintains normalization and compliance, enforces audit trail.

plainFields.name: refund_reason
plainFields.description: Business reason stated for refund request - Implements audit and fulfillment requirements. Atomic value, never derived.

plainFields.name: refund_status
plainFields.description: Status of the refund process (e.g., requested, approved, denied, completed). For business workflow management and normalization.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: When refund was submitted. Used for compliance/audit, not derived.

plainFields.name: processed_at
plainFields.description: When refund was processed/closed. Null if pending.

plainFields.name: admin_note
plainFields.description: Admin-side notes on the refund - Enforces business transparency. Input only, not derived.

models.name: ai_shop_return_requests
models.description: Order item return request entity - Implements the requirement for customer-initiated product returns, maintaining normalized row-per-return structure as required by 3NF. For example, created when a customer requests a return or exchange for an order item. Key relationships: FK to ai_shop_order_items and ai_shop_customers. Return lifecycle is managed at item level for audit precision and inventory control.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Returned order item ({@link ai_shop_order_items.id}). Maintains atomic normalization.

foreignFields.name: requested_by_customer_id
foreignFields.description: FK to requesting customer ({@link ai_shop_customers.id}). Clarifies provenance, audit, and compliance.

plainFields.name: return_reason
plainFields.description: Text of the customer's return reason - Implements the workflow initiation element of return processing. 3NF, atomic, never derived.

plainFields.name: return_status
plainFields.description: Return workflow status (e.g., requested, approved, denied, completed, received). Used in process control. Never derived, atomic.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: When the return was requested. Used for workflow and audit compliance.

plainFields.name: processed_at
plainFields.description: When the return request was processed. Null if pending.

plainFields.name: admin_note
plainFields.description: Admin field for workflow notes and comments (input only, not derived). 3NF.

models.name: ai_shop_order_abandonments
models.description: Abandoned order log - Implements the business requirement to track orders that were initiated but never completed (cart or payment abandoned). 3NF: Each abandonment event is atomic, one row per occurrence; no denormalized or summarized fields. Used to trigger automated retention offers, cart recovery, and behavioral analytics. Key relationships: FK to ai_shop_orders and ai_shop_customers for provenance and audit.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_id
foreignFields.description: Abandoned order ({@link ai_shop_orders.id}). Required to link event and main order data.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id
foreignFields.description: FK to the customer who abandoned the order ({@link ai_shop_customers.id}). For reporting and behavioral analytics.

plainFields.name: abandoned_at
plainFields.description: When the abandonment was registered (cart closed, payment not completed, etc.). Business workflow trigger; atomic, not derived.

plainFields.name: detection_method
plainFields.description: Business code for how/why the abandonment was recognized (e.g., 'timeout', 'payment_fail', 'customer_cancel', 'browser_exit'). Input only, atomic.

models.name: ai_shop_order_deliveries
models.description: Order delivery workflow entity - Fulfills order delivery/logistics requirement from analysis. Each record reflects a delivery event associated with an order. 3NF normalized: one row per delivery event, all fields atomic. For example, created when a seller creates or updates a delivery for an order with shipment information. Key relationships: FK to ai_shop_orders and ai_shop_sellers. May also reference ai_shop_order_items if split delivery is supported (field is optional/null).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_id
foreignFields.description: Related order's {@link ai_shop_orders.id}. For context and access control.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Optionally links for split/partial deliveries ({@link ai_shop_order_items.id}); null for full-order deliveries.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Delivery processing seller ({@link ai_shop_sellers.id}). Required for fulfillment audit trail.

plainFields.name: delivery_status
plainFields.description: Delivery progress status (e.g., pending, ready, shipped, delivered, returned). For workflow and audit. Atomic only, not derived.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Shipper's tracking/parcel number, never calculated. 3NF compliant.

plainFields.name: shipper_code
plainFields.description: Courier company/service code per business policy. For example, 'CJ', 'FEDEX'. Not derived, never aggregated.

plainFields.name: shipped_at
plainFields.description: When parcel left warehouse/seller. Fulfills audit and workflow audit.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: When parcel reached customer. Fulfills audit and customer care business requirements. Null if not delivered.

plainFields.name: seller_memo
plainFields.description: Seller-side memo on the delivery - input only, atomic, never derived.

plainFields.name: admin_note
plainFields.description: Admin auditing/memo field, fully normalized.

models.name: ai_shop_coupons
models.description: Coupon entity - This implements the 'Digital Coupons & Campaign Codes' requirement from the Discount and Payment System requirements. Represents all coupons (single-use, multi-use, stackable or exclusive) available for promotional campaigns, targeted offers, or seller-specific deals. Maintains 3NF compliance. For example, a campaign might generate 10,000 unique coupon codes, all tracked here.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique coupon identifier for lifecycle management, audit, and traceability.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_promotion_id
foreignFields.description: Related promotion's {@link ai_shop_promotions.id}. Nullable if coupon is not part of a campaign.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Coupon code string (unique).

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Coupon type (e.g., 'single_use','multi_use','stackable','exclusive').

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-friendly explanation of the coupon.

plainFields.name: valid_from
plainFields.description: Coupon validation start datetime.

plainFields.name: valid_until
plainFields.description: Coupon expiration datetime.

plainFields.name: max_uses
plainFields.description: Maximum total uses before expiration.

plainFields.name: max_uses_per_customer
plainFields.description: Maximum uses per customer.

plainFields.name: min_purchase_amount
plainFields.description: Minimum order amount for coupon redemption.

plainFields.name: discount_amount
plainFields.description: Absolute discount (e.g., $5 off) or null if only percent.

plainFields.name: discount_percent
plainFields.description: Discount percent (e.g., 10.0 for 10%).

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Current activation status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last updated timestamp.

models.name: ai_shop_coupon_assignments
models.description: Coupon Assignment entity - Implements the requirement 'Assignment, Tracking, Usage Logging' for coupons. Tracks which customer (or entity) has received, claimed, or used a specific coupon. Maintains 3NF by separating assignment and usage from coupon definition. For example, a user redeeming a code will have a row here.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for uniquely identifying each coupon assignment event.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_coupon_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned coupon's {@link ai_shop_coupons.id}.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned or claiming customer's {@link ai_shop_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order's {@link ai_shop_orders.id} where the coupon was applied.

plainFields.name: assigned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when coupon assigned to customer.

plainFields.name: redeemed_at
plainFields.description: Nullable redemption timestamp.

plainFields.name: state
plainFields.description: Assignment state ('assigned', 'redeemed', 'expired', etc.).

models.name: ai_shop_promotions
models.description: Promotion/Campaign entity - Implements the 'Promotion Campaign, Bulk Coupon Creation, and Event Management' requirements. Tracks all coupon campaigns, automatic promotions, manual or AI-driven sales events that govern coupon logic and presentation. Each campaign can generate multiple coupon codes linked via ai_shop_coupons.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Each campaign/promotion's unique identifier.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Promotion title (e.g., 'Summer 2025 Campaign').

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-friendly explanation.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Promotion type ('bulk_coupon', 'auto_discount', 'event', etc.).

plainFields.name: start_at
plainFields.description: Campaign start timestamp.

plainFields.name: end_at
plainFields.description: Campaign end timestamp.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether the campaign is enabled and visible.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Campaign creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for campaign.

models.name: ai_shop_deposits
models.description: Deposit entity - Implements 'Customer/Seller Deposit Tracking and Balance Ledger'. Represents non-withdrawable or redeemable credits in the platform, viewable and manageable per-user. Maintains 3NF. For example, a single credit purchase transaction appears as a row in this table.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique deposit ledger entry.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer making the deposit.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller beneficiary for this deposit (nullable).

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order associated with this deposit (nullable).

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Deposit line type: 'credit','debit','reward', etc.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Deposit transaction amount.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional transaction note.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Ledger entry creation timestamp.

models.name: ai_shop_mileages
models.description: Mileage entity - This implements the 'Mileage Points Tracking' requirement for discount and loyalty. Tracks all atomic accrual or deduction transactions for the mileage (point, loyalty) system tied to a specific customer.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each mileage transaction entry.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer earning or spending mileage points.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order linked to mileage flow (earning/redeeming). Nullable.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Mileage transaction type: 'earn','redeem','adjust','expire', etc.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Change in mileage points (positive or negative).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional note for the points event.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Transaction timestamp.

models.name: ai_shop_donation_coupons
models.description: Donation Coupon entity - Implements the requirements for 'Donation-Linked Coupon Tracking' and compliance with charity-linked transactions. Represents specialized coupons whose use generates (or is funded by) charitable contributions. Normalized to atomic value and relationship per company compliance requirements.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each donation-related coupon entry.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_coupon_id
foreignFields.description: Coupon involved in the donation.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who used the coupon (donor).

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_order_id
foreignFields.description: Related order (if the donation is tied to a purchase). Nullable.

plainFields.name: amount_donated
plainFields.description: Monetary value of donation linked to this coupon redemption.

plainFields.name: donation_type
plainFields.description: Donation linkage type (e.g., 'seller_funded','platform_match','customer_opt_in').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for audit trails and compliance.

models.name: ai_shop_inquiries
models.description:
Inquiry Entity - Implements the core inquiry requirements from the AI Shop Inquiry and Review System requirements analysis (see ERD section). 

This model represents individual product or order inquiries written by customers. It is fully normalized with a direct relationship to the customer making the inquiry and optional linkage to a specific product. Maintains 3NF by only including inquiry-specific attributes; replies and moderation are handled in separate, related tables. Example: A customer submits a question about a product, tracked here for workflow, analytics, and future reference.

Key relationships: belongs to a customer (foreign key to ai_shop_customers) and may reference ai_shop_products. All replies, ratings, and moderation are tracked outside of this entity. 
Special behaviors: Each inquiry is immutable for audit logging, and moderation actions are independently tracked.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each inquiry.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced customer's {@link ai_shop_customers.id}. Indicates the customer who wrote this inquiry.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_product_id
foreignFields.description: Target product's {@link ai_shop_products.id} this inquiry is about, if any.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the inquiry - Implements requirement for clear subject line. This field provides a concise indicator of inquiry content for listing, search, and indexing.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Inquiry content/body - Main question or statement posed by the customer. Normalized as atomic text.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Inquiry status - Implements workflow requirement. Indicates open, resolved, or closed state, used in moderation and escalation flows. Example: 'open', 'answered', 'closed'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the inquiry was created. Required for audit trail and ordering.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update (if any). For mod tracking and data freshness monitoring. Null when never updated.

models.name: ai_shop_inquiry_replies
models.description:
Inquiry Reply Entity - Implements the need for threaded, multi-seller/admin/customer responses to inquiries per requirements and ERD. 

This model is 3NF compliant and stores individual replies to an inquiry, including support for nested replies (threading) via self-referencing parent_id. It allows both sellers and admins to engage customers transparently. 

Key relationships: References ai_shop_inquiries (parent inquiry), ai_shop_sellers, ai_shop_admins; supports hierarchy via parent_id for infinite threading. Usage example: Seller answers a question, followed by further clarification threads.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each reply.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_inquiry_id
foreignFields.description: Parent inquiry's {@link ai_shop_inquiries.id} this reply references.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller user {@link ai_shop_sellers.id} who wrote the reply, if reply is from a seller.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin user {@link ai_shop_admins.id} who wrote the reply, if reply is from an admin.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Self-reference for threaded replies (parent reply). Allows for hierarchical, nested threading of responses.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Reply content/body - Core reply message. Implements business rule for atomic, auditable communication.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reply was made. For chronological ordering, moderation, and SLA measurement.

models.name: ai_shop_reviews
models.description:
Review Entity - Implements the customer product review requirements (see Inquiry & Review requirements and ERD). 

This fully normalized model represents a single customer review on a product, with atomic fields for content, rating score, and extensive linkage to customer and product. Snapshots for moderation/history are tracked separately. 

Compliance: 3NF strictly maintained (no pre-aggregations/denormalizations). Usage example: Customer writes a review for a purchased product, which is then subject to moderation/rating workflows.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the review.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer {@link ai_shop_customers.id} who wrote the review.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product {@link ai_shop_products.id} being reviewed.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Review content/body. The normalized text of the review. Example: Customer's feedback.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Star rating assigned by the customer. Integer value, typically 1-5. Enforces business logic for star-based rating systems.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Moderation or publication status (e.g., 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'). Used in system workflows to separate public/pending reviews.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when review is written. Supports analytics/audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last edit. Nullable if never updated.

models.name: ai_shop_review_moderations
models.description:
Review Moderation Record - Implements review moderation flow (see Inquiry & Review System acceptance criteria). Tracks all moderation actions, linking reviews, admins, and logs. 

Each moderation record is created per action and is fully normalized, separated from review content itself. Enables full audit, compliance tracing, and snapshotting.

Key relationships: References ai_shop_reviews (target), ai_shop_admins (actor/admin), and includes moderation decision, notes, and timestamp. Example: Admin flags or approves a review after AI or human check.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique moderation action record.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_review_id
foreignFields.description: Target review's {@link ai_shop_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin actor {@link ai_shop_admins.id} who took moderation action.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Moderation action ('approve', 'reject', 'flag'). Maps to business rules for platform compliance.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for moderation action. Ensures all actions are auditable and justified. Example: 'Spam', 'Abusive language'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of moderation action; ensures traceability and audit compliance.

models.name: ai_shop_review_ratings
models.description:
Review Helpful/Helpfulness Rating - Implements atomic, per-user (customer) ratings of reviews' helpfulness per requirements document.

Each record logs a single customer's upvote/downvote (e.g., 'helpful' or not) on a specific review, meeting requirements for engagement tracking and feedback loops. Enforces 3NF by storing only atomic user-review vote; any aggregation is handled externally. 

Key relationships: References ai_shop_reviews and ai_shop_customers for each vote instance. Example usage: Customer marks a review as 'helpful', supporting review ranking and display.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique instance of review rating/vote.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_review_id
foreignFields.description: Target review's {@link ai_shop_reviews.id} being rated.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer {@link ai_shop_customers.id} giving the helpfulness rating.

plainFields.name: helpful
plainFields.description: Helpfulness indicator (true for helpful, false for not). Implements binary upvote/downvote pattern per requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the helpfulness vote was registered. Enables feedback recency tracking and abuse mitigation.

models.name: ai_shop_inquiry_moderations
models.description:
Inquiry Moderation Record - Implements moderation tracking requirements for customer inquiries, meeting audit and platform compliance business imperatives.

Each record reflects a moderation action performed by an admin on a specific inquiry, separately from the inquiry content itself. 3NF is maintained by avoiding denormalized outcomes— snapshots and aggregate data managed elsewhere. 

Key relationships: Connects the moderated inquiry, the acting admin, and logs specific action/reason.
Example: An admin flags a question as inappropriate, records action and rationale for audit.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique moderation action instance.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_inquiry_id
foreignFields.description: Moderated inquiry's {@link ai_shop_inquiries.id}.

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin {@link ai_shop_admins.id} performing the moderation.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Moderation action type (e.g., 'approve', 'flag', 'delete'). Mirrors business logic for workflow transitions.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Justification for moderation action. Required for compliance/audit. Example: 'Off-topic', 'Spam', etc.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of moderation action.

models.name: ai_shop_favorites_products
models.description: Product favorites entity - Implements the favorites product feature from the "Favorites System" requirements document. Tracks a customer's favorited products, enabling AI-driven personalized sorting and management. Maintains strict 3NF normalization by keeping atomic relationships (favored product, owning customer) separate from business logic. For example, when a user favorites a product, a record is created here for audit trail and personalization.

primaryField.name: id

foreignFields.name: ai_shop_customer_id

### `ai_shop_channels`

Channel entity - This implements the marketplace channel management requirement from the system architecture documentation. Represents a sales or display channel (e.g., main shopfront, special event shop, mobile app, partner portal). Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic, non-redundant channel information. For example, a separate channel for a Black Friday event can be created and referenced by products, categories, etc. Key relationships: referenced by sections, categories, potentially products in other domains. Special behaviors: channel code must be unique; channel can be enabled/disabled for serving.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each shop channel.
- `code`: Channel code - Implements unique channel identifier requirement. Used for programmatic reference (e.g., 'main', 'event2025'). Ensures normalization by separating channel logic from display names. Example: code='main', code='mobile'. Unique.
- `name`: Channel display name - Implements business need for human-readable identification. Shown in admin/UI selectors. Fully normalized from code. Example: 'Main Shop', 'Mobile Exclusive'.
- `enabled`: Whether this channel is active and visible - Implements channel status management. Enables/disables serving of products/content via this channel. Example: enabled=true for an active channel.
- `sort_order`: Ordering of channels in UI - For business control of display order. Example: sort_order=1 for highest.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of channel creation - Implements audit trail requirement. Normalized as atomic event timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update. For audit and synchronization.

### `ai_shop_sections`

Section entity - Implements the marketplace section management requirement from the system architecture document. Represents a logical grouping within a channel (e.g., home, sale, electronics landing). Maintains 3NF by separating section info from channel, category, display logic. Example: A 'Deals' section in 'main' channel. Key relationships: references ai_shop_channels via channel_id. Special behaviors: section code is unique within channel.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each shop section.
- `ai_shop_channel_id`: Parent channel's [ai_shop_channels.id](#ai_shop_channels) - Connects section to its parent channel, enforcing referential integrity.
- `code`: Section code (unique within channel) - Business need for programmatic reference. Example: 'home', 'products', 'outlet'.
- `name`: Section name for display in UI - Human-readable identifier. Example: 'Homepage', 'Outlet'.
- `sort_order`: Ordering of sections within a channel - Controls display sequence.
- `enabled`: Whether section is active.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of section creation.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp.

### `ai_shop_configurations`

Platform configuration entity - Implements global/system configuration requirement from architecture documentation. Each row is a single configuration parameter (name-value pair), enabling dynamic and scalable platform settings. Maintains strict normalization (no redundant or precomputed settings). Example: max_cart_size, maintenance_mode. Can be used by system at runtime. Special behaviors: param_name unique.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each configuration parameter.
- `param_name`: Configuration parameter name - Implements atomic, normalized key/value store of platform configuration. Example: 'max_cart_size', 'maintenance_mode'. Unique.
- `param_value`: Value for the configuration parameter - May be stringified JSON for complex settings. Example: 'true', '50', '{"allowed":true}'.
- `description`: Human-readable description of what this config controls. Assists admin understanding, auditing. Example: 'The maximum number of items allowed in a cart.'
- `created_at`: Timestamp when configuration was created. Enables auditing, rollback, compliance with 3NF.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp.

### `ai_shop_categories`

Category entity - Implements category taxonomy/management requirement from system documentation. Represents hierarchical or flat categories used in product organization, navigation, filtering. Maintains full 3NF normalization by having explicit parent_id for trees and linking only via foreign keys. Example: 'Electronics' (parent=null), 'Laptops' (parent=Electronics ID). Key relationships: references ai_shop_channels for scoping to channel; parent_id for nesting. Special behaviors: unique per channel + code. Distributed (multi-tenant) shops supported.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique for each category.
- `ai_shop_channel_id`: Channel containing this category [ai_shop_channels.id](#ai_shop_channels). Enables multi-channel support for categories.
- `parent_id`: Parent category's [ai_shop_categories.id](#ai_shop_categories) (can be null for root categories). Implements hierarchical taxonomy as required. Null for category roots.
- `code`: Category code (unique within channel, for this tree level) - For programmatic use. Example: 'electronics', 'shoes'.
- `name`: Category display name - UI/admin view. Example: 'Laptops'.
- `sort_order`: Position/display order among siblings. Used for drag-sort in admin UIs. Example: sort_order=4 for 4th in parent.
- `enabled`: Whether category is shown to end-users. For blacklist/hiding logic. Example: 'enabled' = false hides everywhere.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of category creation. Ensures auditability and history.
- `updated_at`: Time last updated.

### `ai_shop_files`

File entity - Implements file management requirement for all uploads in the platform (systematic, product, bulletin, user, etc.). Enables normalized, auditable file storage and access metadata. Maintains 3NF: links to nothing, stores only atomic file data. Example: a product image, a user-uploaded attachment. Key relationships: referenced via file_id by attachments, images, etc., in other domains. Special behaviors: store both original file name and unique storage URI; unique uri enforced.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique file identifier.
- `original_name`: Original file name as uploaded - For UI/admin display. Example: 'invoice2025.pdf'.
- `uri`: Persistent storage URI or path (e.g., cloud url, s3 key). For programmatic file retrieval. Example: 'files/2025/07/report.pdf'. Unique.
- `mime_type`: File mime type, e.g., image/png, application/pdf. Used for preview, content validation.
- `size_bytes`: Size of file in bytes. For auditing, quota enforcement. Example: 51288.
- `uploader_name`: Name of uploader (if available at upload time).
- `uploaded_at`: Timestamp when file was uploaded. Audit and traceability.

### `ai_shop_audit_logs`

Audit log entity - Implements platform-wide audit and compliance logging, as per architecture compliance documentation. Maintains normalized logs: each change, action, or critical event is a row. Provides traceability for GDPR, disputes, admin intervention. Normalized to ensure no event denormalization or aggregation. Example: order status change log, admin action log. Can be used to reconstruct user or system activity. Key relationships: none in this domain, but could reference user/seller/admin IDs in other domains. Special behaviors: event_id unique for deduplication; event_type indexed for fast filtering.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Log entry identifier.
- `event_id`: Unique event identifier for idempotency/deduplication. Example: 'ORD20250722-38'.
- `event_type`: Event type code (e.g., 'USER_LOGIN', 'ORDER_CANCELED', 'CONFIG_EDIT'). Used for fast querying and filtering.
- `actor_id`: Actor identifier (references user, seller, admin, etc. in other domains). Nullable for system-initiated events.
- `actor_role`: Role of actor, e.g., 'customer', 'seller', 'admin', or null for system.
- `target_table`: Table affected by event, for traceability. Example: 'ai_shop_orders'.
- `target_id`: Row/entity affected, allows for multi-entity logging without foreign key enforcement.
- `details`: Detailed JSON blob (as string) describing event content, before/after states. Example: '{"from":"pending","to":"paid"}'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when event occurred, precise to at least 1 second.

### `ai_shop_customers`

AI Shop Customer Entity - This implements customer identity, onboarding, and profile core requirements from the Customer Management spec. Business Purpose: Represents end-users (buyers). Links to profile; authentication base. Maintains 3NF normalization; preference/secondary contacts in profile. Example: Used in onboarding and customer login. Key relationships: 1:1 with ai_shop_customer_profiles. Special: GDPR, deletion, audit required.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Globally unique customer identifier.
- `email`: Customer Email. Primary login and contact identity. Unique and required. Example: For notifications and login.
- `phone`: Customer Phone Number. For notifications or MFA. Optional.
- `status`: Lifecycle/account status (active/withdrawn/suspended). Used for access control. Required. Application-level enum.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of account creation.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update.

### `ai_shop_sellers`

AI Shop Seller Entity - implements onboarding and approval processes for marketplace sellers. Business Purpose: Represents merchant identity (legal/business), separate from product or inventory. Follows 3NF; all contact details in profile. Example: Onboarding reviewed by admin. Key: 1:1 with ai_shop_seller_profiles. Special: Approval required, audit logs tracked.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique seller identifier.
- `business_name`: Official Store/Business Name. Used in public shop, invoice, and admin review. Required and unique.
- `business_registration_number`: Business Registration Number, government ID/legal identifier. Unique.
- `status`: Account (onboarding/active/suspended) status. Controls access. Enum at app layer.
- `approved_at`: Timestamp when admin approved this seller. Nullable if not yet reviewed.
- `created_at`: When seller started onboarding.
- `updated_at`: When seller account was last updated.

### `ai_shop_admins`

AI Shop Admin Entity - implements storage for platform/admin users. Business purpose: Used for management, onboarding, audit/logging, admin privileges. 3NF; admin-specifics in separate profile. Used in audit logs, permission checks. One-to-one with ai_shop_admin_profiles. Special: High-security; audit required.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key. Unique, non-sequential admin identity.
- `username`: Unique admin username for login and audit tracing. Required.
- `status`: Admin account status (active/suspended/pending). Access control.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for admin account creation.
- `updated_at`: Latest update timestamp for admin account.

### `ai_shop_auth_providers`

AI Shop Auth Provider mapping for external login/OAuth/2FA association for all actor types. Business: Links customer, seller, or admin to social/OAuth/email/multi-factor. 3NF: provider linkage is always separate from credentials. Example: Google login, or SMS 2fa, 1:many with actors. Special: All FKs within actor tables; unique per (provider_type, external_id, [actor_id]).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key. Unique linkage record.
- `customer_id`: Customer FK - links to ai_shop_customers.id if provider for a customer.
- `seller_id`: Seller FK - links to ai_shop_sellers.id if associated with seller.
- `admin_id`: Admin FK - links to ai_shop_admins.id if associated with admin.
- `provider_type`: Type (google/kakao/apple/naver/email/totp/sms/etc). Required.
- `external_id`: External (provider) unique user id.
- `linked_at`: Timestamp when linkage established. Required.

### `ai_shop_user_sessions`

AI Shop User Session table - tracks login/concurrent session/audit for any customer, seller, or admin. All FKs within actor tables. Used to control history, forced logout, device management. Special: Session FK to a single actor; allows multiple concurrent per user. 3NF. Example: Forced logout sets terminated_at.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key. Unique session context.
- `customer_id`: FK to customer for session. Nullable.
- `seller_id`: FK to seller for session. Nullable.
- `admin_id`: FK to admin for session. Nullable.
- `session_token`: Login token. Unique per session. Required.
- `issued_at`: Session creation timestamp.
- `expires_at`: Expiration timestamp. Required.
- `terminated_at`: If forcibly ended, the timestamp here. Nullable.
- `ip_address`: Session IP address (for audit/tracing). Required.

### `ai_shop_customer_profiles`

AI Shop Customer Profile - extended preferences, contacts, addresses, privacy for each customer. All profile data separate from core customer for 3NF. Key: 1:1 to ai_shop_customers. Used for personalization, GDPR and preference data. Special: Nullable fields for optional attributes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key. Unique profile identity.
- `customer_id`: FK to ai_shop_customers.id, enforced unique (1:1).
- `name`: Full customer name for address and display. Required.
- `preferences`: Serialised preferences JSON. Optional.
- `dob`: Date of birth (if collected for compliance/age). Optional.
- `gender`: Gender for analytics/marketing (nullable, optional).
- `locale`: Language/locale code (fr, ko, en...). Optional.
- `shipping_addresses`: Serialized multi-address JSON. Optional, for customer with multi-ship support.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when profile created.
- `updated_at`: Last profile update.

### `ai_shop_seller_profiles`

AI Shop Seller Profile - all extended seller business/contact details for compliance/audit. All contacts and documents here; seller table only core legal ID info. Key: 1:1 to ai_shop_sellers. Used for onboarding, KYC, compliance review.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key. Unique seller profile identity.
- `seller_id`: FK to ai_shop_sellers.id, enforced unique (1:1).
- `contact_name`: Primary legal/business contact name. Required.
- `contact_email`: Contact email (distinct from login/business email). Required.
- `company_phone`: Business phone (for compliance, shipping, support). Optional.
- `address`: Business address. Used for legal/compliance. Optional.
- `kyc_documents`: JSON list of attached/additional files or KYC uploads (referenced to file storage system). Optional.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when seller profile record created.
- `updated_at`: Last update to seller profile.

### `ai_shop_admin_profiles`

AI Shop Admin Profile - admin-specific duty or contact extensions. Only for admin; distinct from core record. Used for compliance assignment, IP allowlist. Key: 1:1 to ai_shop_admins. Special: Compliance allows for optional/blank values in duty region, IP list.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key. Unique admin profile identity.
- `admin_id`: FK to ai_shop_admins.id, enforced unique (1:1).
- `duty_region`: Compliance jurisdiction/region assigned to this admin. Optional.
- `ip_allowlist`: JSON array of approved IPs or CIDR ranges (for compliance); nil if unrestricted.
- `contact_email`: Backup/admin notification or escalation email; optional.
- `created_at`: Profile created timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last profile update timestamp.

### `ai_shop_products`

AI Shop Product - Implements requirements for product management as described in the requirements (core registration, management, AI-driven enrichment, and auditability). Strictly normalized (3NF), with options, variant, tags, inventory, images all separated. All edit/version history in ai_shop_product_snapshots. Business example: a seller creates a new product for sale. Key relationships: owned by seller (FK), references category. Special: supports soft deletion and full audit trail.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique product record identifier.
- `ai_shop_seller_id`: Belonged seller's [ai_shop_sellers.id](#ai_shop_sellers). Each product belongs to a seller, enforcing business accountability and permissions.
- `category_id`: Category assignment for product (requirement: catalog classification). Normalized FK to ai_shop_categories.
- `name`: Product name/title. Implements requirement for registration. Maintains 3NF—text is stored here, not duplicated. Example: 'Eco Bag Large'.
- `description`: Product description (rich text/HTML/markdown). Implements content display, AI enrichment. Example: 'A stylish eco bag with spacious main compartment.'
- `status`: Current product status. Enum: 'active','inactive','draft','suspended','deleted'. Controls visibility. Example: 'active'.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp. Used for audit, analytics. Maintains 3NF.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for audit and analytics.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp; NULL if active. For compliance and audit. Optional.

### `ai_shop_product_variants`

Product Variant - Implements support for multi-option/variant combo SKUs, as required for e-commerce product management. Example: Red-Large variant of a product. Maintains 3NF by holding only atomic data for SKU identification and linkage to parent product. Key relationship: belongs to exactly one product (FK). Example: Variant for bag in red, size L.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_product_id`: Parent product reference [ai_shop_products.id](#ai_shop_products). Each variant links to its owner product.
- `sku`: Stock-Keeping Unit for logistics/integration. Must be unique for product+variant combo. Example: 'SKU-BAG-RED-L'.
- `option_combo`: Atomic string encoding of option combination (e.g., 'Color:Red;Size:L').
- `barcode`: Barcode (EAN/UPC/QR) for scanning/inventory. Example: '8809876543210'. Nullable, not always required.
- `is_active`: Whether this variant can be sold. Example: true.

### `ai_shop_inventories`

Inventory - Tracks the stock for each product variant, enabling inventory management, restock alerting, and audit trail. Strictly 3NF: one inventory per variant, all adjustments logged externally. Relationships: belongs to seller (FK), belongs to variant (1-1, unique). Example: stock of 25 items for SKU-RED-L.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_product_variant_id`: Product variant for this inventory item - FK to [ai_shop_product_variants.id](#ai_shop_product_variants). 1:1 unique join.
- `ai_shop_seller_id`: Seller owning this inventory record (for audit/control) [ai_shop_sellers.id](#ai_shop_sellers).
- `stock`: Current stock quantity for this variant. Example: 10 units.
- `restock_threshold`: Stock threshold at which restock alert triggers. Example: 3.
- `turnover_rate`: Rate of sales for this variant per day/week/month. Used for AI-driven analytics. Example: 2.45 units/day.
- `created_at`: Inventory record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp for audit/analytics.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp. Null if not deleted.

### `ai_shop_product_snapshots`

Product Snapshot - Provides versioning and full edit/audit traceability for compliance, rollback, and business analytics. Strictly normalized: each snapshot records all atomic fields, with no denormalized data. Snapshots are linked to a product and timestamped. Example: reverting product to previous content after mistake or dispute. Key relationship: belongs to a product.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_product_id`: Parent product for this snapshot (FK to ai_shop_products.id).
- `name`: Name of product as of this snapshot, for rollback and audit. Example: 'Eco Bag Large'.
- `description`: Product description as of this snapshot, for audit trail. Strictly atomic for rollback. Example: 'A stylish eco bag with spacious main compartment.'
- `category_id`: Category at snapshot time. Used for rollback and compliance tracking.
- `status`: Product status at this snapshot state (e.g., 'active').
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp, not product creation date.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot record was last updated.

### `ai_shop_product_images`

Product Images - Stores and organizes product images for gallery use, with URI, alt text, and gallery order/position. Strictly 3NF. Each image references a single product. Example: Main image for 'Eco Bag'.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_product_id`: Parent product for this image (FK to ai_shop_products.id).
- `image_uri`: URI or location of the image file. Example: 'https://cdn.ai-shop.com/images/bag1.jpg'.
- `alt_text`: Alt text for image accessibility compliance.
- `position`: Gallery index/position in image ordering. Example: 1.

### `ai_shop_product_tags`

Product Tag - Logical assignment of search/tag labels to products. Tags are atomic labels for search/AI-driven user experience and cross-sell. Strictly 3NF—no derived summaries or denormalized aggregates. Each record is a product-tag association, with unique constraint. Example: Tag on 'Eco Bag' as 'eco-friendly'.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_product_id`: Product this tag is assigned to (FK to ai_shop_products.id).
- `tag_text`: Atomic tag label. Example: 'eco-friendly'.
- `created_at`: When the tag was created.

### `ai_shop_product_import_logs`

Product Import Log - Tracks all bulk import or batch product registration events. Used for audit, error tracking, and integration. Strictly normalized with explicit fields only. Key relationship: references seller of the import operation. Example: import of 100 SKUs from csv.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_seller_id`: Seller who performed import event (FK to ai_shop_sellers.id).
- `imported_at`: When the import completed.
- `source_file`: URI to source batch file or import artifact.
- `record_count`: Number of products handled in the import event.
- `status`: Import operation status. Enum: 'pending','completed','failed'.
- `error_message`: Import failure or error reason; nullable, only populated on error.

### `ai_shop_carts`

Shopping Cart Entity - Implements the persistent cart requirement from the Cart and Order System document (Section 4, Functional Requirements #1, #3).

This model represents a logical shopping cart associated primarily with a customer or a guest session. Its business purpose is to enable the platform to store a user's intended purchases across sessions, devices, and authentication states. It ensures 3NF normalization by storing only the cart container and its metadata; specific cart item details are normalized into ai_shop_cart_items. For example, when a customer adds products to their shopping cart, this entity records the top-level cart record, trackable by customer_id or cart_session_id.

Key relationships: Links to ai_shop_cart_sessions (if unauthenticated), and to ai_shop_customers (for authenticated users; foreign key to be defined from Actors schema). Maintains audit fields and status for cart lifecycle (active, abandoned, converted, etc).
Special behaviors: Cart is unique to either a customer or a session, never both, supporting both registered and guest flows.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each shopping cart.
- `ai_shop_customer_id`: Belonged customer's [ai_shop_customers.id](#ai_shop_customers). Nullable for guest carts. This links a shopping cart directly to a registered customer account for persistent, cross-device cart experience.
- `ai_shop_cart_session_id`: Belonged cart session's [ai_shop_cart_sessions.id](#ai_shop_cart_sessions). Used for unauthenticated/guest carts.
- `status`: Cart status flag - Implements the requirement for lifecycle tracking (active, abandoned, converted). Business meaning: tracks the primary cart state for abandonment processing and analytic triggers. Normalized here as a single atomic value. E.g., 'active', 'abandoned'.
- `created_at`: Cart creation timestamp. Used for audit trails and tracking cart staleness/abandonment for compliance and customer service. 3NF-compliant atomic timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Cart last updated timestamp. Enables precise cart lifecycle management, normalization preserved.
- `abandoned_at`: Timestamp of when the cart was considered abandoned. Implements compliance and business abandonment requirements. Nullable as only set when cart is abandoned.

### `ai_shop_cart_items`

Shopping Cart Item Entity - Implements the normalized itemization requirement from Cart and Order System document (Functional Requirements #1, #3, #4).

This entity stores each product/variant line in a shopping cart, supporting full 3NF normalization. Business purpose: allows for precise separation of cart container and contained product selections. For example, each entry represents a single SKU/variant the customer intends to buy, with quantity and option/variant references.

Key relationships: Belongs to ai_shop_carts, references ai_shop_products and ai_shop_product_variants (from Products schema) to ensure referential integrity for catalog links. Normalized: NO product names/prices stored here. Example usage: add-to-cart API inserts a record per selected product variant, quantity, and options. Special behaviors: Each cart can have many items, each item unique by product/variant constraints.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each cart item.
- `ai_shop_cart_id`: Belonged cart's [ai_shop_carts.id](#ai_shop_carts). Links item to its parent cart for proper containment and lifecycle management.
- `ai_shop_product_id`: Product reference's [ai_shop_products.id](#ai_shop_products). Enforces product-level referential integrity. Normalized - only stores reference, not product data.
- `ai_shop_product_variant_id`: Product variant reference's [ai_shop_product_variants.id](#ai_shop_product_variants). Ensures atomic relationship at SKU/variant granularity. No denormalized attribute data.
- `quantity`: Quantity of the product variant requested. Implements the atomic, normalized representation of product choices. Always ≥ 1. E.g., user selects 2 of a certain size/color.
- `added_at`: When the cart item was added. Business purpose: enables time-based cart, inventory, and promotional analytics. Maintains normalization as atomic value.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for cart item. Useful for tracking changes (e.g., quantity updates). Still atomic and normalized.

### `ai_shop_cart_sessions`

Cart Session Entity - Addresses the session-linked cart requirement from Cart and Order System (Functional Requirement #1 and architectural needs).

Business purpose: enables persistent cart storage for unauthenticated/guest users using a session-unique token. Maintains normalization by only recording the link to the guest session. When a user logs in, their session cart can be migrated to their account cart. For example, a new visitor adds items to a cart and is tracked via this record until authentication. Audit trail fields enable lifecycle and analytic monitoring.

Key relationships: Optionally linked to ai_shop_carts (1:1), not directly to products or customers. Used for session-based cart flows. Special behaviors: Carts can be migrated/merged between guest sessions and user accounts based on business rules.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this cart session.
- `session_token`: Unique session token issued to guest/unregistered users to identify cart sessions. Implements guest cart persistence. Atomic value; not reused or denormalized.
- `created_at`: Creation time for the cart session. Audit/compliance requirement.
- `updated_at`: Last update time for the session's activity/lifecycle. Enables analysis and cart synchronization.

### `ai_shop_orders`

Order entity - This implements the primary order management requirement from the Cart and Order System requirements. Captures the full business-to-customer transaction lifecycle, including customer linkage, cart association, seller involvement, pricing, and order audit. 3NF compliance: Only atomic, normalized data (no pre-calculated totals). For example, when a customer checks out a cart, an ai_shop_orders record is created with all relevant FK links. Key relationships: Linked to ai_shop_customers, ai_shop_carts, ai_shop_sellers, and item, delivery, refund entities.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_customer_id`: Belonged customer's [ai_shop_customers.id](#ai_shop_customers)
- `ai_shop_seller_id`: Seller's [ai_shop_sellers.id](#ai_shop_sellers) for single-seller orders, or main seller in multi-seller scenario
- `ai_shop_cart_id`: Associated cart's [ai_shop_carts.id](#ai_shop_carts) for order provenance
- `order_number`: Order human-readable identifier - Implements traceability for the business and customers. 3NF: not derived from other columns, strictly assigned at order creation. E.g. 'ORD20240722-0001'.
- `status`: Current order business status (e.g., pending, paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) - Implements state management. Not derived. Usage: for process control and audit.
- `submitted_at`: Timestamp when order was placed - Implements audit/compliance requirements. Not derived data. Used to track order creation moment.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp - For auditing order state progression. Not derived; is updated by workflow actions.
- `payment_method`: Selected payment method code (e.g., 'card', 'deposit', 'coupon'). Fulfills checkout and compliance requirement. Not derived from other entities.
- `customer_memo`: Customer's memo for the order (e.g., delivery instructions) - Direct input, atomic, not derived.
- `admin_note`: Internal admin memo about the order - 3NF: for audit/admin use only, not shown externally. Input only, not derived.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion flag: timestamp if deleted, null otherwise. For audit and compliance, enables logical deletes.

### `ai_shop_order_items`

Order item detail - Implements the order line-items requirement from the Cart and Order System plan. Each row represents a distinct item within an order (SKU-level). Fully normalized (3NF): no derived subtotals or aggregates; each field corresponds directly to atomic input or reference. Used, for example, to list each purchased product with its variant, quantity, and price at purchase time. Key relationships: Foreign keys to ai_shop_orders and ai_shop_products/variants.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_order_id`: Parent order's [ai_shop_orders.id](#ai_shop_orders) - Required for item linkage.
- `ai_shop_product_id`: Purchased product's [ai_shop_products.id](#ai_shop_products) - 3NF; atomic reference for business reporting.
- `ai_shop_product_variant_id`: Variant of the product's [ai_shop_product_variants.id](#ai_shop_product_variants). Enables SKU-level granularity and atomic normalization.
- `product_name`: Snapshot of the product name at purchase. Implements audit/traceability. Not derived; direct input. Example: 'AI Smart Speaker v2'.
- `variant_name`: Optional: Variant display name for audit. Not derived; direct.
- `quantity`: Quantity of this product/variant purchased.
- `unit_price`: Unit price at time of purchase (after discounts, if any). Fulfills audit and compliance; no calculations, atomic only.
- `currency`: Currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'KRW') at sale time. Required for international operations; not derived.
- `seller_memo`: Memo field for seller-side item note. Not derived; audit use. Example: 'Special packing'.

### `ai_shop_order_status_histories`

Order state change log - Implements the audit/compliance snapshot from requirements: logs every change in ai_shop_orders.status. Maintains full normalized snapshot history. For example, a new row is added whenever the order status transitions (e.g., from 'pending' to 'paid'). Key relationships: Foreign key to ai_shop_orders. Special behaviors: Immutable records, always append-only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_order_id`: Reference to the affected [ai_shop_orders.id](#ai_shop_orders). For access path and integrity.
- `changed_by_admin_id`: Optional reference to admin who performed the update. For compliance and traceability ([ai_shop_admins.id](#ai_shop_admins)).
- `from_status`: Previous status value - For audit trail, normalization 3NF: not derived.
- `to_status`: New status value - For audit trail.
- `changed_at`: Timestamp of change event. Not derived; audit evidence. Atomic property.
- `change_reason`: Optional admin/editor reason for status change. Fulfills requirement for business auditing. Not derived.

### `ai_shop_order_refunds`

Order refund request entity - Fulfills the requirement for explicit tracking of refund requests and processing from the requirements analysis. 3NF compliance: only atomic, factual attributes are stored for each refund. Used, for instance, when a buyer requests a refund for an order item. Key relationships: FK to ai_shop_orders.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_order_id`: Refunded order's [ai_shop_orders.id](#ai_shop_orders). For traceability and workflow enforcement.
- `requested_by_customer_id`: FK to customer who requested refund ([ai_shop_customers.id](#ai_shop_customers)). Maintains normalization and compliance, enforces audit trail.
- `refund_reason`: Business reason stated for refund request - Implements audit and fulfillment requirements. Atomic value, never derived.
- `refund_status`: Status of the refund process (e.g., requested, approved, denied, completed). For business workflow management and normalization.
- `requested_at`: When refund was submitted. Used for compliance/audit, not derived.
- `processed_at`: When refund was processed/closed. Null if pending.
- `admin_note`: Admin-side notes on the refund - Enforces business transparency. Input only, not derived.

### `ai_shop_return_requests`

Order item return request entity - Implements the requirement for customer-initiated product returns, maintaining normalized row-per-return structure as required by 3NF. For example, created when a customer requests a return or exchange for an order item. Key relationships: FK to ai_shop_order_items and ai_shop_customers. Return lifecycle is managed at item level for audit precision and inventory control.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_order_item_id`: Returned order item ([ai_shop_order_items.id](#ai_shop_order_items)). Maintains atomic normalization.
- `requested_by_customer_id`: FK to requesting customer ([ai_shop_customers.id](#ai_shop_customers)). Clarifies provenance, audit, and compliance.
- `return_reason`: Text of the customer's return reason - Implements the workflow initiation element of return processing. 3NF, atomic, never derived.
- `return_status`: Return workflow status (e.g., requested, approved, denied, completed, received). Used in process control. Never derived, atomic.
- `requested_at`: When the return was requested. Used for workflow and audit compliance.
- `processed_at`: When the return request was processed. Null if pending.
- `admin_note`: Admin field for workflow notes and comments (input only, not derived). 3NF.

### `ai_shop_order_abandonments`

Abandoned order log - Implements the business requirement to track orders that were initiated but never completed (cart or payment abandoned). 3NF: Each abandonment event is atomic, one row per occurrence; no denormalized or summarized fields. Used to trigger automated retention offers, cart recovery, and behavioral analytics. Key relationships: FK to ai_shop_orders and ai_shop_customers for provenance and audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_order_id`: Abandoned order ([ai_shop_orders.id](#ai_shop_orders)). Required to link event and main order data.
- `ai_shop_customer_id`: FK to the customer who abandoned the order ([ai_shop_customers.id](#ai_shop_customers)). For reporting and behavioral analytics.
- `abandoned_at`: When the abandonment was registered (cart closed, payment not completed, etc.). Business workflow trigger; atomic, not derived.
- `detection_method`: Business code for how/why the abandonment was recognized (e.g., 'timeout', 'payment_fail', 'customer_cancel', 'browser_exit'). Input only, atomic.

### `ai_shop_order_deliveries`

Order delivery workflow entity - Fulfills order delivery/logistics requirement from analysis. Each record reflects a delivery event associated with an order. 3NF normalized: one row per delivery event, all fields atomic. For example, created when a seller creates or updates a delivery for an order with shipment information. Key relationships: FK to ai_shop_orders and ai_shop_sellers. May also reference ai_shop_order_items if split delivery is supported (field is optional/null).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shop_order_id`: Related order's [ai_shop_orders.id](#ai_shop_orders). For context and access control.
- `ai_shop_order_item_id`: Optionally links for split/partial deliveries ([ai_shop_order_items.id](#ai_shop_order_items)); null for full-order deliveries.
- `ai_shop_seller_id`: Delivery processing seller ([ai_shop_sellers.id](#ai_shop_sellers)). Required for fulfillment audit trail.
- `delivery_status`: Delivery progress status (e.g., pending, ready, shipped, delivered, returned). For workflow and audit. Atomic only, not derived.
- `tracking_number`: Shipper's tracking/parcel number, never calculated. 3NF compliant.
- `shipper_code`: Courier company/service code per business policy. For example, 'CJ', 'FEDEX'. Not derived, never aggregated.
- `shipped_at`: When parcel left warehouse/seller. Fulfills audit and workflow audit.
- `delivered_at`: When parcel reached customer. Fulfills audit and customer care business requirements. Null if not delivered.
- `seller_memo`: Seller-side memo on the delivery - input only, atomic, never derived.
- `admin_note`: Admin auditing/memo field, fully normalized.
